reading: The interior of the 6-coloured rectangular outline is filled with the colour of the other (small) object, and that small object is erased.

slots.container: interior of the one rectangular outline object (frame)
slots.paint: colour of the other, non-frame object
slots.source: the non-frame object, which is cleared to background

why: frame interior becomes the donor colour; donor cells become background; frame unchanged

reading: The input is scaled up by a factor equal to the number of non-background colours; then colour-2 diagonals run from each corner of the scaled interior block outward through background until a non-background cell or the border.

slots.factor: number of distinct non-background colours in the input
slots.subject: the interior (non-edge) object block after scaling
slots.line: diagonal rays of colour 2 from each of its box corners, outward, over background only, stopping at border or non-background

why: output = input scaled by colour count, plus 2-diagonals from the inner block's corners

reading: Each coloured cell at odd coordinates (2i+1, 2j+1) becomes a 4x4 block at (4i, 4j) in a 20x20 output (downsample by 2, upscale by 4).

slots.lattice: input cells at odd row and odd column
slots.factor: each lattice cell becomes a 4x4 block (net scale x2)

why: output block (i,j) has the colour of input cell (2i+1,2j+1)

reading: The shape in the top-left panel (cut by the cross separator) is recoloured to the separator colour and mirrored into four quadrants (original, left-right flip, up-down flip, both); the separator is removed.

slots.unit: top-left panel of the separator cross
slots.layout: 2x2 of unit, flipped horizontally / vertically / both, separator dropped

why: output is the 4-fold symmetric arrangement of the recoloured top-left panel

reading: The input is colour-inverted (background and the one foreground colour swap) and the inverted grid is tiled 2x2.

slots.unit: input with its two colours swapped

why: every output block equals the swapped-colour input

reading: The 8-coloured shape is cut out as a 3x3 box and repeated side by side horizontally once for each colour-4 marker cell in the input.

slots.count: number of isolated colour-4 marker cells

why: output = 3 x (3*k) with k copies of the shape box, k = number of 4-markers

reading: Vertical 8-bars come in lengths 2,4,6,8,10; one bar has its half coloured 9. That 9 half reverts to 8 and the same end-half (top or bottom) of the next-longer bar is coloured 9.

slots.marked: vertical segment whose top or bottom half is colour 9
slots.target: the segment whose length is the next larger than the marked one
slots.paint: the same end-half of the target becomes 9; the marked half becomes 8

why: exactly one bar carries a 9 half; it moves one step up the length order, keeping which end it is on

reading: The 3x3 input is placed into a 9x9 grid at every block whose corresponding input cell has the least frequent colour; other blocks are empty.

new_rows.name: rare
new_rows.datalog:
ccount(C, count(Y, X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
least(min(N)) :- ccount(C, N).
rare(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), ccount(C, N), least(M), N = M.

why: block (i,j) is a copy of the input iff input cell (i,j) has the minimum colour count, else all 0
invariants: the unit is the unchanged input

reading: The coloured rows at the top are reflected to the bottom about the grid's horizontal midline.
why: output is symmetric about the horizontal centre line of the grid; original rows kept

reading: The single marker cell fills, in its own colour, the rectangle spanning from it to the grid corner nearest to it.

new_rows.name: corner_box
new_rows.datalog:
hm(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
wm(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
rowsel(Y) :- cell(MY, MX, C), hm(H), D = H - MY, MY < D, px(Y, X, K), Y1 = MY + 1, Y < Y1.
rowsel(Y) :- cell(MY, MX, C), hm(H), D = H - MY, D < MY, px(Y, X, K), Y0 = MY - 1, Y > Y0.
colsel(X) :- cell(MY, MX, C), wm(W), D = W - MX, MX < D, px(Y, X, K), X1 = MX + 1, X < X1.
colsel(X) :- cell(MY, MX, C), wm(W), D = W - MX, D < MX, px(Y, X, K), X0 = MX - 1, X > X0.
corner_box(Y, X) :- rowsel(Y), colsel(X).

why: every cell between the marker and its nearest grid corner (inclusive) takes the marker colour; nothing else changes
